# Illustrating the 'httr2' functions

```{r slide08}
httr2::request("https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json") |>
  httr2::req_url_query("$limit" = 5) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

```

## FRED Example

```{r}
ohio_jobs = 
httr2::request("https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
    file_type = "json"
  ) |>
  # nothing has been sent yet
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

ohio_df = ohio_jobs$observations # we saw that the data is in observations

# another approach to filter the dates would be:
ohio_df |> 
  # overwrite the date col and convert to date (from chr)
  dplyr::mutate(date = lubridate::ymd(date)) |> 
  # because it is a date, we can do logical checks on it and it keeps dates from sep 1 2026
  dplyr::filter(date >= '2026-09-01') -> ohio_df_sept_2026

```

## USA Jobs

```{r usajobs}
httr2::request("https://data.usajobs.gov/api/search") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(Keyword = "Data Analyst", ResultsPerPage = 500) |>
  httr2::req_headers(
    Host = "data.usajobs.gov",
    "User-Agent" = "papandaj@miamioh.edu",
    "Authorization-Key" = Sys.getenv("USA_API_KEY")
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(flatten = TRUE) -> usa_jobs_data


usa_jobs_df = usa_jobs_data$SearchResult$SearchResultItems

jobs_small = usa_jobs_df |> 
  dplyr::select(
    title = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle,
    department = MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName,
    agency = MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName,
    location = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionLocationDisplay,
    closes = MatchedObjectDescriptor.ApplicationCloseDate
  )

## Easy way -- since we looked for data analyst as a key word
nrow(jobs_small)
# q 2
table(jobs_small$department) |> sort(decreasing = T)
jobs_small |> dplyr::count(department) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) |> head(3)

## the harder way but being literal
jobs_small |> dplyr::filter(title == 'Data Analyst') -> count_literal


## the harder way without being literal
index_data_analyst = jobs_small$title |> 
  stringr::str_detect("Data Analytics|Data Analyst")

#given that this is a true or false type result
# true rows will be kept
# , nothing means keep all col
count_standard = jobs_small[index_data_analyst , ]

```
